s0601.literal: The Qing Shan rebel barbarians Hong gelao and others submitted and still presented local products as tribute; each was granted gold and silk.
s0601.idiomatic: The Qing Shan rebel barbarians Hong gelao and others submitted and still presented local products as tribute; each was granted gold and silk.

s0602.literal: Wujiang Prefecture suffered great flooding and the people lacked food; ten thousand shi of rice were issued for relief.
s0602.idiomatic: Wujiang Prefecture suffered great flooding and the people lacked food; 10,000 shi of rice were issued for relief.

s0603.literal: Eleventh month, on jisi day the imperial carriage returned to Dadu.
s0603.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jisi day, the imperial carriage returned to Dadu.

s0604.literal: On xinwei day Jupiter transgressed Fang.
s0604.idiomatic: On xinwei day Jupiter transgressed Fang.

s0605.literal: On renshen day the moon transgressed Emptiness.
s0605.idiomatic: On renshen day the moon transgressed Emptiness.

s0606.literal: On jiaxu day Mars transgressed Neck.
s0606.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Mars transgressed Neck.

s0607.literal: On dinghai day Wuchang Route suffered fire; one month's grain was granted to those affected by the disaster.
s0607.idiomatic: On dinghai day Wuchang Route suffered fire; one month's grain was granted to those affected by the disaster.

s0608.literal: On wuzi day Mars transgressed Root.
s0608.idiomatic: On wuzi day Mars transgressed Root.

s0609.literal: On xinmao day the moon transgressed Mars.
s0609.idiomatic: On xinmao day the moon transgressed Mars.

s0610.literal: On bingshen day the households under Prince Anxi Ananda and Prince Xiping Oljei were all short of food; rice was granted in varying amounts.
s0610.idiomatic: On bingshen day the households under Prince Anxi Ananda and Prince Xiping Oljei were all short of food; rice was granted in varying amounts.

s0611.literal: Yidu, Yangzhou, and Chenzhou suffered famine that year; more than twenty-one thousand shi of grain were sold at reduced prices for relief.
s0611.idiomatic: Yidu, Yangzhou, and Chenzhou suffered famine that year; more than 21,000 shi of grain were sold at reduced prices for relief.

s0612.literal: Twelfth month, on renyin day Venus appeared in daylight.
s0612.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renyin day, Venus appeared in daylight.

s0613.literal: On yisi day Jupiter transgressed Eastern Winnowing.
s0613.idiomatic: On yisi day Jupiter transgressed Eastern Winnowing.

s0614.literal: On renzi day thirteen stations including Suoge Ch'er lacked food; grain was granted for three months.
s0614.idiomatic: On renzi day 13 stations including Suoge Ch'er lacked food; grain was granted for three months.

s0615.literal: On yimao day the Emperor was ill; slaughter throughout the empire was forbidden for forty-two days.
s0615.idiomatic: On yimao day the Emperor was ill; slaughter throughout the empire was forbidden for 42 days.

s0616.literal: On bingchen day Xuanzheng Bureau commissioner Shadi and others were dispatched to pray at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
s0616.idiomatic: On bingchen day Xuanzheng Bureau commissioner Shadi and others were dispatched to pray at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

s0617.literal: The households under Prince He'er Bandaa scattered and fled; an edict warned that wherever anyone dared conceal them would be punished.
s0617.idiomatic: The households under Prince He'er Bandaa scattered and fled; an edict warned that wherever anyone dared conceal them would be punished.

s0618.literal: On wuwu day the moon transgressed Root.
s0618.idiomatic: On wuwu day the moon transgressed Root.

s0619.literal: On guihai day Wang Wenhe, chief of Napeng Cave in Lin'gao County, Qiongzhou, and others rose in rebellion and were executed upon capture.
s0619.idiomatic: On guihai day Wang Wenhe, chief of Napeng Cave in Lin'gao County, Qiongzhou, and others rose in rebellion and were executed upon capture.

s0620.literal: Tian Yuntong of Cizhou, who had murdered his mother, was dismembered and displayed in the marketplace.
s0620.idiomatic: Tian Yuntong of Cizhou, who had murdered his mother, was dismembered and displayed in the marketplace.

s0621.literal: That year, forty-four persons were sentenced to death.
s0621.idiomatic: That year, 44 persons were sentenced to death.

s0622.literal: Eleventh year, spring, first month, on the bingyin new moon, the Emperor was critically ill; court congratulations were waived.
s0622.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, on the bingyin new moon of the first month of spring, the Emperor was critically ill; court congratulations were waived.

s0623.literal: On guiyou day he died in the Yude Hall; he had reigned thirteen years and lived to forty-two.
s0623.idiomatic: On guiyou day he died in the Yude Hall; he had reigned 13 years and lived to 42.

s0624.literal: On yihai day the imperial bier set out; he was buried at Qilian Valley, following the imperial tombs.
s0624.idiomatic: On yihai day the imperial bier set out; he was buried at Qilian Valley, following the imperial tombs.

s0625.literal: That year, ninth month, on yichou day the posthumous title was Qinming Guangxiao Emperor; the temple name was Chengzong; in the national language he was styled Emperor Wanze Du.
s0625.idiomatic: That year, in the ninth month, on yichou day the posthumous title was Qinming Guangxiao Emperor; the temple name was Chengzong; in the national language he was styled Emperor Wanze Du.

s0626.literal: Chengzong, inheriting after the empire had been unified under Heaven, ruled with hands folded in the sleeves — one may say he was skilled at preserving what had been achieved.
s0626.idiomatic: Chengzong, inheriting after the empire had been unified under Heaven, ruled with hands folded in the sleeves — one may say he was skilled at preserving what had been achieved.

s0627.literal: Yet in his final years illness afflicted him year after year; all state affairs — within the palace they were decided by the empress's curtain, without they were entrusted to the chief ministers;
s0627.idiomatic: Yet in his final years illness afflicted him year after year; all state affairs — within the palace they were decided by the empress's curtain, without they were entrusted to the chief ministers;

s0628.literal: Yet that the dynasty did not fall to ruin was because Shizu had not long departed and the established statutes remained fully in force.
s0628.idiomatic: Yet that the dynasty did not fall to ruin was because Shizu had not long departed and the established statutes remained fully in force.
